Tuvan People's Republic: Mongolian. The Tuvan People's Republic (TPR), known simply as Tuva, was a partially recognized socialist republic that existed between 1921 and 1944 in North Asia.

Anastas Mikoyan was Soviet statesman and revolutionary (1895–1978).
This former bureaucrat turned anti-corruption activist won a Ramon Magsaysay Award in 2006, then became the 7th Chief Minister of Delhi — who is he?
Arvind Kejriwal (Hindi; born 16 August 1968) is an Indian politician, activist and former bureaucrat, who served as the 7th Chief Minister of Delhi.
In 751, an Abbasid-Tibetan force defeated Tang China's army for control of territory near the Syr Darya, ending Tang expansion into Central Asia — which clash?
Battle of Talas (pinyin: Dlus Zhny) was an armed confrontation between the Abbasid Caliphate along with the Tibetan Empire against the Tang dynasty and its allies in 751.
Guided by ten principles like radical inclusion and radical self-reliance, this week-long event climaxes with the torching of a giant wooden effigy in Nevada's Black Rock Desert — what is it?
Burning Man is a week-long large-scale desert event focused on "community, art, self-expression, and self-reliance" held annually in the Western United States.

Born among the Tugen of the Rift Valley and once a schoolteacher, which man became Kenya's longest-serving president, ruling from 1978 to 2002?
Daniel arap Moi (2 September 1924 - 4 February 2020) was a Kenyan politician who served as the second president of Kenya from 1978 to 2002.

Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) is a South African communist and black nationalist political party.

Eve is a figure from the Book of Genesis in the Old Testament.

Gabby Giffords (born June 8, 1970) is an American retired politician and gun violence prevention advocate.

This American politician has served as the 48th Governor of Texas since 2015, after stints as state attorney general and a justice on the Texas Supreme Court, making him the nation's longest-serving incumbent governor — who is he?
Greg Abbott (born November 13, 1957) is an American politician, attorney, and jurist who has served since 2015 as the 48th governor of Texas.
This German chancellor's 16-year tenure — the longest in the country's post-war history — spanned the end of the Cold War, German reunification, and the founding of the European Union — who is he?
Helmut Kohl (3 April 1930 - 16 June 2017) was a German politician who served as chancellor of Germany and governed the Federal Republic from 1982 to 1998.
This Venezuelan leader renamed his country the "Bolivarian Republic" and gave his name to a whole political ideology before dying in office in 2013 — who was he?
Hugo Chávez (28 July 1954 - 5 March 2013) was a Venezuelan politician, revolutionary, and military officer who was the president of Venezuela from 1999 until his death in 2013.
The eldest son of a former U.S. president and first lady, this businessman and environmentalist ran as the Democratic nominee in Nevada's 2006 Senate election — who is he?
Jack Carter (politician) (born July 3, 1947) is an American businessman, politician and environmentalist.
Before becoming U.S. secretary of defense in 2017, this Marine Corps four-star general led both U.S. Central Command and NATO's Supreme Allied Command Transformation — who is he?
Jim Mattis (born September 8, 1950) is an American military officer who served as the 26th United States secretary of defense from 2017 to 2019.
A mountain range on Pluto and an asteroid both bear her name — fitting for the Japanese climber who was the first woman atop Everest and the first to bag the Seven Summits. Who was she?
Junko Tabei (ne Ishibashi; 22 September 1939 - 20 October 2016) was a Japanese mountaineer, author and teacher.
Carved out of a former Electorate after Napoleon dissolved the Holy Roman Empire in 1806, this southern German monarchy lasted until 1918 — which one?
Kingdom of Württemberg was a German state that existed from 1806 to 1918, occupying territory in what is now the southern German federal state of Baden-Wrttemberg.

Born from the anti-authoritarian faction that split from the Marxists within the International Workingmen's Association, this political tradition champions workers' self-management while rejecting the state — what is it called?
Libertarian socialism is an anti-authoritarian and anti-capitalist political current that emphasises self-governance and workers' self-management.

A Chinese revolutionary and political theorist who founded the People's Republic of China in 1949, he adapted Marxism to the Chinese context in a theory now known by his name. Who led from 1949 until his death in 1976?
Mao Zedong (26 December 1893 - 9 September 1976) was a Chinese revolutionary, politician, writer, political theorist and the founder of the People's Republic of China (PRC).
Named after a 16th-century Frisian cleric who was a contemporary of Martin Luther, these Anabaptist Christian communities trace their roots to the Radical Reformation — who are they?
Mennonites are a group of Anabaptist Christian communities tracing their roots to the epoch of the Radical Reformation.

In Hindu tradition it's the highest of life's four aims — above dharma, artha, and kama — and across Jainism, Buddhism, and Sikhism it names liberation from the cycle of death and rebirth. What is it?
Moksha (UK also), also called vimoksha, vimukti, and mukti, is a term in Jainism, Buddhism, Hinduism, and Sikhism for various forms of emancipation, liberation, nirvana, or release.

Nguyễn Khánh (8 November 1927 - 11 January 2013) was a Vietnamese military officer and politician.
This giant huntsman of Greek myth was placed among the stars by Zeus or Artemis, and one legend even credits him with carving out the shape of the Strait of Sicily — who is he?
Orion (mythology) (: Ancient) was a giant huntsman whom Zeus or Artemis placed among the stars as a constellation.
A member of Vietnam's Politburo since 2016 and once the Party Secretary of Quảng Ninh province, this politician became his country's eighth prime minister in 2021 — who is he?
Phạm Minh Chính (born 10 December 1958) is a Vietnamese politician and former public security lieutenant general.

Ramesses I was the founding pharaoh of ancient Egypt's 19th Dynasty. The dates for his short reign are not completely known but the timeline of late 1292–1290 BC is frequently cited as well as 1295–1294 BC.

Arguing that cheaper letters would mean more letters and thus higher profits, this English teacher and reformer championed a Uniform Penny Post and is credited with inventing the postage stamp — who was he?
Rowland Hill (3 December 1795 - 27 August 1879) was an English teacher, inventor and social reformer.

Semyon Timoshenko was Soviet military commander (1895–1970).

Vicente Fox (Latin American; born 2 July 1942) is a Mexican businessman and politician who served as the 62nd president of Mexico from 2000 to 2006.
This Ohioan holds a singular distinction: he is the only person to have served as both U.S. president and chief justice of the United States. Who was he?

Christian VII: King of Denmark and Norway from 1766 to 1808.

Corporatism: Political ideology which advocates the organization of society by corporate groups.

Domitian: Roman emperor from AD 81 to 96.

Efraín Ríos Montt: 38th President of Guatemala from 1982 to 1983.

Erik the Red: Norse explorer. According to Icelandic sagas, Erik was born in the Jæren district of Rogaland, Norway, the son of Thorvald Asvaldsson.

Freemasonry consists of fraternal groups that trace their origins to medieval guilds of stonemasons, and is considered the oldest existing secular fraternal organisation, with documents and traditions dating back to the 14th century.

House of Habsburg: European dynastic family.

John Diefenbaker: Prime Minister of Canada from 1957 to 1963. John George Diefenbaker (September 18, 1895 – August 16, 1979) was the 13th prime minister of Canada, serving from 1957 to 1963.

Rising from vice president after Bingu wa Mutharika's death, she became the first female president of Malawi in 2012 and only the second woman to lead an African nation, after Liberia's Ellen Johnson Sirleaf — who is she?

Joyce Banda: President of Malawi from 2012 to 2014. Joyce Hilda Banda (née Ntila; born 12 April 1950) is a Malawian politician, educator, and activist who served as the fourth president of Malawi from 2012 to 2014.

Katipunan: Filipino secret society during the Spanish colonization.

One of the original five Marshals of the Soviet Union, this military officer and politician later served as the country's head of state from 1953 to 1960, having forged a close friendship with Stalin during the Battle of Tsaritsyn — who was he?
Kliment Voroshilov: Soviet military officer and politician (1881–1969)
This Norse explorer is believed to have reached continental North America roughly five centuries before Columbus, establishing a settlement he called Vinland — who is he?

Louis Bonaparte: King of Holland from 1806 to 1810. Louis Bonaparte (born Luigi Buonaparte; 2 September 1778 – 25 July 1846) was a younger brother of Napoleon I, Emperor of the French.
This Northern Irish peace activist co-founded a movement seeking a peaceful end to the Troubles, sharing the 1976 Nobel Peace Prize with Betty Williams — who is she?
Mairead Maguire: Northern Irish peace activist (born 1944)

Nefertari: Wife of the Egyptian pharaoh Ramesses II.

Nyx: Ancient Greek goddess of the night. In ancient Greek art, Nyx often appears alongside other celestial deities such as Selene, Helios and Eos, as a winged figure driving a horse-pulled chariot.

At age 89 in 2023, this Spanish economist and former Communist politician was proposed as a prime ministerial candidate in a Vox-led no-confidence vote — who is he?
Ramón Tamames: Spanish economist and politician. Ramón Tamames Gómez (born 1 November 1933) is a Spanish economist and former politician.

Saul: Biblical figure and Israelite monarch.
In Hinduism, what name is given to the feminine 'Universal Power' that complements Shiva and is worshipped at shrines called pithas?
Shakti: Divine feminine energy in Hinduism.

Sino-Vietnamese War: War between China and Vietnam in 1979.
This Indonesian general became his country's second president in 1967, two years after his troops put down an attempted coup — who is he?
Suharto: President of Indonesia from 1967 to 1998.

Temple in Jerusalem: Former places of Israelite and Jewish worship.

The illegitimate son of Mircea I of Wallachia, this nobleman was inducted into the Order of the Dragon in 1431 and twice ruled Wallachia as Voivode in the 1430s and 1440s — who is he?
Vlad II Dracul: Ruler of Wallachia (r. 1436–1442, 1443–1447)
Introduced to the public in 1954 by a retired British civil servant, this modern pagan, Earth-focused religion blends ancient motifs with 20th-century hermetic ideas — which religion?
Wicca: Modern syncretic pagan religion. Wicca draws upon ancient pagan and 20th-century hermetic motifs for theological and ritual purposes.

After his father — a former Andhra Pradesh chief minister — died in a 2009 helicopter crash, this politician toured the state on a consoling 'Odarpu Yatra' before founding his own party and later becoming chief minister himself — who is he?

Y. S. Jagan Mohan Reddy: Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh, India. Jagan Mohan Reddy started his political career in the Indian National Congress and was elected as the Member of Parliament of Kadapa in 2009.
This ancient Iranian faith centers on the Avesta and reveres Ahura Mazda as the supreme, uncreated deity, teaching a struggle between Asha (truth) and Druj (the lie). What religion is it?
Zoroastrianism: Iranian religion founded by Zoroaster.
Which one below was born first?
Joseph Schumpeter (born 1883) is the earliest of the four. Joseph Alois Schumpeter (German: [ˈʃʊmpeːtɐ]; February 8, 1883 – January 8, 1950) was an Austrian political economist.
Who among these was born first?
Patrick Geddes (born 1854) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these was founded earliest?
Bash (Unix shell) (founded 1989) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below was established earliest?
Fortran (founded 1957) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these is a physicist?
Which of these is a chemist?
Ellen Swallow Richards is a chemist. Richards graduated from Westford Academy (second oldest secondary school in Massachusetts) in 1862.
What is the atomic number of Moscovium?
Moscovium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Mc and atomic number 115.
What is the atomic number of Bismuth?
Bismuth is a chemical element; it has symbol Bi and atomic number 83.
In what year did Marie Curie die?
Marie Curie: Curie was born in Warsaw, Russian Empire, where she studied at the clandestine Flying University and began her practical scientific training.
In what year was Sodium discovered?
Sodium is a chemical element; it has symbol Na (from Neo-Latin natrium) and atomic number 11.
Ammonium chloride: Pfizer. Ammonium chloride is an inorganic chemical compound with the chemical formula NH4Cl, also written as [NH4]Cl.
Boeing 777X: United States. The Boeing 777X is an American long-range, wide-body, twin-engine airliner built by Boeing Commercial Airplanes, undergoing flight testing.
Who is credited with discovering Telescopium?
Telescopium: Nicolas Louis de Lacaille. Its name is a Latinized form of the Greek word for telescope.
Who is credited with discovering Spontaneous generation?
Spontaneous generation: Anaximander. It was hypothesized that certain forms, such as fleas, could arise from inanimate matter such as dust, or that maggots could arise from dead flesh.
Who is credited with discovering SN 1987A?
SN 1987A: Ian Shelton. SN 1987A was a Type II supernova in the Large Magellanic Cloud, a dwarf satellite galaxy of the Milky Way.
This Onmyōdō master advised Heian emperors on astrology and spiritual matters; a Kyoto shrine and an Osaka train station now honor him — who is he?
Abe no Seimei (February 21, 921 AD - October 31, 1005) was a Japanese onmyji, a court official and specialist of Onmyd, during the middle of the Heian period.
First approved in the United States in 1966, this xanthine oxidase inhibitor treats high uric acid levels linked to gout, kidney stones, and chemotherapy — what medication is it?
Allopurinol is a medication used to decrease high blood uric acid levels.
Nicknamed 'the heart of the scorpion,' this distinctly reddish variable star is the brightest in the constellation Scorpius — what is it?
Antares is the brightest star in the constellation of Scorpius. It has the Bayer designation α Scorpii, which is Latinised to Alpha Scorpii.

Named for the Ancient Greek word for 'star' after its flower shape, this group of roughly 170 mostly Eurasian perennial plants is also known for its late-blooming 'Michaelmas daisies' — which plant group?
Aster (genus) is a genus of perennial flowering plants in the family Asteraceae.
Once chairman of the Nasdaq, this financier admitted to masterminding the largest-known Ponzi scheme in history, estimated at $65 billion — who was he?

Bernie Madoff (April 29, 1938 - April 14, 2021) was an American financier, con artist, and stock broker who was the admitted mastermind of the largest-known Ponzi scheme in history, worth an estimated $65 billion.
This family of cloven-hoofed, ruminant mammals includes cattle, bison, buffalo, antelopes, sheep, and goats across 143 living species — name the family?
Bovidae is the biological family of cloven-hoofed, ruminant mammals that includes cattle, bison, buffalo, antelopes, and goat-antelopes such as sheep and goats.
Sole living family in the mammalian suborder Tylopoda, which group unites camels with llamas and their South American relatives?
Camelidae is a family of mammals belonging to the ungulate order Artiodactyla (even-toed ungulates) and the only living family in the suborder Tylopoda.
A secondarily aquatic clade within the order that also includes hippos, this infraorder covers whales, dolphins and porpoises, along with extinct relatives like Basilosaurus — which group of animals?

Cetacean are marine mammals belonging to the infraorder Cetacea, a secondarily aquatic clade under the order Artiodactyla that include whales, dolphins, porpoises and extinct groups such as Basilosaurus.

From a tree in the myrtle family, these dried flower buds from the Moluccas are harvested year-round across different countries and lend their scent to everything from cosmetics to cooking — what are they?
Clove are the aromatic flower buds of a tree in the family Myrtaceae, Syzygium aromaticum.

This naturally occurring but largely inactive steroid hormone shields organs like the kidneys from active cortisol, and gets converted back into cortisol by an enzyme mainly in the liver — what hormone is it?
Cortisone is a naturally occurring, mostly inactive pregnene (21-carbon) steroid hormone.
The word names both a noun — a plan or proposal made by a thinking agent — and a verb for developing one, always aiming to satisfy goals while weighing function and aesthetics; what is it?
Design is the concept or proposal for an object, process, or system.
This soil-dwelling invertebrate of the phylum Annelida is also known by slang names like 'dew-worm,' 'rainworm,' and 'nightcrawler.' What creature is it?
Earthworm is a soil-dwelling terrestrial invertebrate that belongs to the phylum Annelida.

A German Jew who fled the Nazi regime for the United States, this social psychologist and psychoanalyst co-founded a New York psychiatric institute and was associated with the Frankfurt School of critical theory — who is he?
Erich Fromm (March 23, 1900 - March 18, 1980) was a German-American social psychologist, psychoanalyst, sociologist, humanistic philosopher, and democratic socialist.
Bred in Brazil as a guard dog, cattle herder, and big-game hunter, this large mastiff-type breed was also once used to catch runaway slaves — which breed?
Fila Brasileiro (Portuguese) is a Brazilian breed of large working dog of mastiff type.

Cataloged by the astronomer Ptolemy in the second century AD and still one of the 88 modern constellations, this zodiac constellation takes its Latin name from the mythological twins Castor and Pollux — what's the constellation?
Gemini (constellation) is one of the constellations of the zodiac and is located in the northern celestial hemisphere.

Native to the Amazon basin, this climbing plant's coffee-bean-sized seeds can contain up to 6% caffeine — roughly double the concentration found in green coffee beans — and flavor a popular Brazilian soft drink. Name the plant?
Guarana (from the Portuguese guaran; Paullinia cupana, syns.

This colorless, nearly odorless organic compound is a straight-chain alkane with six carbon atoms, widely used as a cheap, largely unreactive solvent and found in small amounts in modern gasoline blends — what is it?
Hexane is an organic compound, a straight-chain alkane with six carbon atoms and the molecular formula C6H14.
This medical condition occurs when the body, or a region of it, is deprived of adequate oxygen at the tissue level — what is it called?

Hypoxia (medicine) is a condition in which the body or a region of the body is deprived of an adequate oxygen supply at the tissue level. Hypoxia may be classified as either generalized, affecting the whole body, or local, affecting a region of the body.

This English mathematician made foundational contributions to matrix and invariant theory, founded the American Journal of Mathematics at Johns Hopkins, and was teaching at Oxford when he died. Who was he?
James Joseph Sylvester (3 September 1814 - 15 March 1897) was an English mathematician.

The first woman of Indian origin to fly to space, this astronaut and aerospace engineer first studied in India before earning advanced degrees in the US and flying aboard Space Shuttle Columbia in 1997 — who was she?
Kalpana Chawla (July 1, 1962 - February 1, 2003) was an Indian-American astronaut and aerospace engineer who was the first woman of Indian origin to fly to space.
This small Arctic rodent is a key prey source for tundra carnivores and is the subject of a persistent myth that it marches off cliffs in mass suicide — what animal is it?
Lemming is a small rodent, usually found in or near the Arctic in tundra biomes.
Named for a Dutch physicist, this six-parameter family of linear equations converts spacetime coordinates between reference frames moving at constant relative velocity — what is it?
Lorentz transformation are a six-parameter family of linear transformations from a coordinate frame in spacetime to another frame that moves at a constant velocity relative to the former.

A student of Marie Curie, this French physicist discovered a new element in 1939 by purifying lanthanum laced with actinium, and went on to become the first woman elected to the French Académie des Sciences — who was she?
Marguerite Perey (19 October 1909 - 13 May 1975) was a French physicist and a student of Marie Curie.

This American theoretical physicist and science communicator, a professor at the City College of New York, won a 2021 lifetime achievement award named for a famous science-fiction author, honoring his work bridging science and sci-fi. Who is he?
Michio Kaku (born January 24, 1947) is an American theoretical physicist, science communicator, futurologist, and writer of popular science.
Scholars can't even agree on which elements define it, yet it appears in every human society as a vehicle for creativity through composition and performance — what is it?
Music is the arrangement of sound to create some combination of form, harmony, melody, rhythm, or otherwise expressive content.
A highly corrosive mineral compound with the formula HNO3, this strong inorganic acid is colorless but yellows over time as it decomposes. What is this acid?
Nitric acid is an inorganic compound with the formula HNO3. The compound is colorless, but samples tend to acquire a yellow cast over time due to decomposition into oxides of nitrogen.
This systemic skeletal disorder develops when the rate of bone breakdown outpaces new bone formation with age, leaving bones porous, less dense, and prone to fracture — what's the condition called?
Osteoporosis is a systemic skeletal disorder characterized by low bone mass, micro-architectural deterioration of bone tissue leading to more porous bone, and consequent increase in fracture risk.
Brought on by too little niacin, this disease announces itself with the 'three D's' — dermatitis on sun-exposed skin, diarrhea, and dementia — what is it?
Pellagra is a disease caused by a lack of the vitamin niacin (vitamin B3).
Which condition, more common in people with obesity or a family history, involves hair and skin debris being drawn into tissue through tiny skin openings called pits?
Pilonidal disease is a type of skin infection that typically occurs as a cyst between the cheeks of the buttocks and often at the upper end.

This corticosteroid drug treats a huge range of conditions — from rheumatoid arthritis and asthma to eye inflammation and certain cancers — and can be taken orally, injected, or applied to the skin. What is it?
Prednisolone is a corticosteroid, a steroid hormone used to treat certain types of allergies, inflammatory conditions, autoimmune disorders, and cancers, electrolyte imbalances, and skin conditions.
This root vegetable in the mustard family, whose entire plant (leaves included) is edible, was domesticated in Asia and is now grown worldwide — what vegetable is it?
Radish (Raphanus sativus or Raphanus raphanistrum subsp.
This big, sociable black corvid is told apart from its relatives by a bare, whitish patch on its face, and it nests in noisy treetop colonies near farms and villages — which bird is it?
Rook (bird) (Corvus frugilegus) is a member of the family Corvidae in the passerine order of birds.

These pinnipeds, distinguished from true seals by their external ear flaps and ability to walk on all fours, belong to the eared-seal family alongside fur seals, with six living species worldwide. What animal is this?
Sea lion are pinnipeds characterized by external ear flaps, long foreflippers, the ability to walk on all fours, short and thick hair, and a big chest and belly.

Named from an Ancient Greek word for 'soap,' this cheesy secretion of shed skin cells, oils, and moisture collects under the foreskin in males and around the folds of female genitalia — what is it called?
Smegma (from Ancient Greek, smgma, 'soap') is a cheesy substance composed of shed skin cells, skin oils, and moisture that occurs in male and female mammalian genitalia.
A Canadian cognitive psychologist at Harvard who champions evolutionary psychology and the computational theory of mind, which popular-science author wrote on how children learn irregular verb forms?
Steven Pinker (born September 18, 1954) is a Canadian cognitive psychologist, psycholinguist, popular science author, and public intellectual.
This protective cap of repetitive nucleotide sequences guards the ends of eukaryotic chromosomes from progressive degradation — what is it called?
Telomere (from Ancient Greek (tlos) 'end' and (mros) 'part') is a region of repetitive nucleotide sequences associated with specialized proteins at the ends of linear chromosomes (see Sequences).
Divided into the thorax, abdomen, and pelvis, this core section of the body is where the head, neck, and all four limbs attach — which body part?
Torso is the central part, or the core, of the body of many animals (including human beings), from which the head, neck, limbs, tail and other appendages extend.
Measuring under five feet long, this critically endangered porpoise is endemic to a small corner of Mexico's Baja California coast — which species?
Vaquita (v-; Phocoena sinus) is a species of porpoise endemic to the northern end of the Gulf of California in Baja California, Mexico.
Inspired by the code-breaking game Mastermind, this once-a-day puzzle gives you six tries and colored tiles to crack the same word everyone else is solving — which game?
The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom
Wordle is a web-based word game created and developed by the Welsh software engineer Josh Wardle.

This organic compound functions as a neurotransmitter in the brain and body of many animal types, including humans. It is the chemical that motor neurons release at the neuromuscular junction to enable muscle movement. What is it?
Acetylcholine: Organic chemical and neurotransmitter. Its name is derived from its chemical structure: it is an ester of acetic acid and choline.
Born in 1929 and died in 2001, this man was a respected Saudi Islamic scholar — who is he?

Native to South Africa's Western Cape, this flowering bulb genus lends its common name to popular winter houseplants that actually belong to a different genus, Hippeastrum — which bulb, also called the naked lady or Jersey lily?
Amaryllis: Genus of plants. Amaryllis is the only genus in the subtribe Amaryllidinae (tribe Amaryllideae).
Named from Greek words for 'curved' and 'vertebra,' this type of arthritis causes long-term inflammation where the spine meets the pelvis — what is it?
Ankylosing spondylitis: Type of arthritis of the spine. Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is a type of arthritis from the disease spectrum of axial spondyloarthritis.
Known commonly as palms, this family of over 2,600 flowering plant species includes climbers, shrubs, and tree-like forms mostly found in the tropics — what's the family called?
Arecaceae: Palm family of flowering plants.
This genus of early African hominins, which lived during the Pliocene and Early Pleistocene, is considered ancestral to the genus that includes modern humans — which genus?
Australopithecus: Genus of hominin ancestral to modern humans. The genera Homo (which includes modern humans), Paranthropus, and Kenyanthropus evolved from some Australopithecus species.
This inflammatory condition causes recurring, painful mouth sores along with eye inflammation and arthritis, and is diagnosed after at least three sore outbreaks in a year — which condition?
Behçet's disease: Inflammatory disorder. Behçet's disease or Behçet's syndrome (BD; sometimes written Behcet) is a type of inflammatory disorder which affects multiple parts of the body.
Rich in vitamin C and polyphenols, this deciduous shrub's glossy dark berries are cooked into jams and syrups or fermented into cassis — what is it?
Blackcurrant: Species of flowering plant in the gooseberry family Grossulariaceae.

This infraorder of decapod crustaceans tucks a stubby tail-like abdomen under a hard shell and ends its front pair of legs in pincers — over 1.5 million tonnes of them are eaten by humans yearly. What group is it?
Brachyura: Crustacean. The true crabs are the largest of the crab decapod groups with carcinised body forms.
A cole crop related to broccoli, cauliflower and Brussels sprouts, the heaviest recorded head of this leafy vegetable weighed nearly 138 pounds — what is it?
Cabbage: Leafy vegetable in the flowering plant family Brassicaceae.
This infraorder of decapod crustaceans is the true taxonomic home of what everyone actually calls a shrimp, found in fresh and salt water worldwide — what is it?
The largest part of the brain, this structure houses the cerebral cortex plus the hippocampus and basal ganglia, and works with the cerebellum to control every voluntary action. What is it?
Cerebrum: Large part of the brain containing the cerebral cortex.
Selected from over 11,000 applicants for NASA's Teacher in Space Project, this Concord, New Hampshire educator died aboard the Challenger in 1986 — who was she?
Christa McAuliffe: American teacher and astronaut (1948–1986)
Found naturally in the sap of the opium poppy, this opiate is a prodrug of morphine often paired with paracetamol to treat mild pain, coughs, and even diarrhea — what is it?
Codeine: Opiate and prodrug of morphine used to treat pain. It usually starts working after half an hour, with maximum effect at two hours.
Caused by a fungus that forms galls on maize plants, this disease produces an edible delicacy in Mexico known as huitlacoche, often stuffed into quesadillas — which condition?
Corn smut: Fungal plant disease on maize and teosinte.
Also called Bermuda grass, this hardy warm-climate turf species is ironically not native to the island of the same name — which plant, by its scientific name?
Cynodon dactylon: Species of grass. Cynodon dactylon, commonly known as Bermuda grass or as couch grass in Australia and New Zealand, is a grass found worldwide in warm and tropical climates.
This central nervous system stimulant is the 'right-handed' mirror-image form of a well-known molecule, prescribed for ADHD and narcolepsy and sometimes given as an inactive prodrug — what is it?
Dextroamphetamine: CNS stimulant and isomer of amphetamine.
A broad-spectrum member of the tetracycline class, this antibiotic treats everything from acne and chlamydia to Lyme disease and cholera — though it'll make you sunburn more easily. Which drug?
Doxycycline: Tetracycline-class antibiotic. It is used to treat bacterial pneumonia, acne, chlamydia infections, Lyme disease, cholera, typhus, and syphilis, and is sometimes used to prevent malaria.
Despite its name, this South American freshwater fish is actually a knifefish, not a true eel, and produces powerful discharges using specialized tissue — which species?
Electrophorus electricus: South American electric fish. It is considered as a freshwater teleost which contains an electrogenic tissue that produces electric discharges.
This flowering shrub in the family Erythroxylaceae is one of only two species whose leaves are cultivated to produce a notorious stimulant — which plant is it?
Erythroxylum coca: Species of flowering plant.
Sporting an orange-red breast rimmed in grey and brown upperparts, this small insect-eating songbird ranges from Western Siberia to North Africa — which bird?
European robin: Species of bird. It is found across Europe, as far east as Western Siberia, and as far south as North Africa.

Boldly patterned in black and yellow to warn predators of its toxicity, this European amphibian can live for more than 50 years and is now vulnerable due to an introduced fungal disease — what species is it?
Fire salamander: Species of amphibian. The fire salamander (Salamandra salamandra) is a common species of salamander found in Europe.
Traditionally pounded from cassava, plantains, and cocoyam, this West African staple gets a shoutout in Chinua Achebe's novel Things Fall Apart — what dish is it?
Fufu: Dough-like food in African cuisine.
The largest of its family, this mostly solitary mammal uses long foreclaws to dig into nests and a sticky tongue to slurp up ants and termites — what animal is it?
Giant anteater: Species of mammal. The giant anteater (Myrmecophaga tridactyla) is an insectivorous mammal native to Central and South America.
One of China's 'Four Great Domestic Fish,' this herbivorous freshwater species was later introduced to Europe and the US to control aquatic weeds — which fish?
Grass carp: Species of fish. This Asian carp is the only species of the genus Ctenopharyngodon.

This prehensile, multi-fingered body part sits at the end of primates' forelimbs — koalas famously have two opposable thumbs on each one, while raccoons are often said to have them despite lacking true opposable thumbs. What is it?
Hand: Extremity at the end of an arm or forelimb.

First synthesized in 1940 by chemist Roger Adams via hydrogenation of THC isomers, this psychoactive cannabis-derived compound is sold in vaporizers despite never being drug-approved — which compound?
Lightest and most abundant element in the universe, it makes up about 75% of all normal matter and fuels the stars — colorless, odorless, and highly combustible. What element is it?
Hydrogen: Chemical element with atomic number 1 (H)
Equal to one-twelfth of a foot and derived from the Roman word for 'twelfth,' this unit of length has been pegged to exactly 25.4 millimeters since the mid-20th century — what is it?
Inch: Unit of length. The inch (symbol: in or ″) is a unit of length in the British Imperial and the United States customary systems of measurement.
Appointed FBI director by Barack Obama in 2013, this former federal prosecutor was fired from the post in 2017 — who is he?
Back in 1859, this Irish physicist proved the link between atmospheric CO2 and what we now call the greenhouse effect — who was he?
A pastor's son and theoretical physicist, this man passed Manhattan Project secrets to the Soviets, served nine years in a British prison, then resumed his science career in East Germany. Who is he?
Klaus Fuchs: German-born British physicist and atomic spy (1911–1988)
Formulated in 1834, this principle of electromagnetism states that an induced current always flows in a direction that opposes the very change in magnetic field that created it — which principle?
Lenz's law: Electromagnetic opposition to change.
Nicknamed "Connie" and instantly recognizable by its triple tail and dolphin-shaped fuselage, which four-engined airliner was the first civil aircraft family to widely use a pressurized cabin?
Lockheed Constellation: Family of US airliners with 4 piston engines, 1943.
This marsupial family native to Australia and New Guinea includes kangaroos, wallabies, and the quokka among its 63 recognized species — what is it?
Macropodidae: Family of marsupial mammals. Macropodidae is a family of marsupials that includes kangaroos, wallabies, tree-kangaroos, wallaroos, pademelons, the quokka, and several other groups.
A Zainichi Korean entrepreneur, this founder and CEO of SoftBank turned a $20 million bet on Alibaba in 2000 into a stake worth around $75 billion — who is he?
Developed in 1955 and later sold under the brand name Dianabol, this anabolic steroid was once widely used for physique and performance enhancement — what is it?
Metandienone: Androgen and anabolic steroid. It is also used non-medically for physique- and performance-enhancing purposes.
Normally equal to 60 seconds, which unit of time has occasionally run 61 seconds long in UTC due to leap seconds, though a 59-second version has never actually occurred?
Minute: Unit of time equal to 60 seconds. The prime symbol ′ is also sometimes used informally to denote minutes.
Also known as green gram, this legume is a staple ingredient across East, Southeast, and South Asian cuisine in both savory and sweet dishes — what is it?
Discovered in 1898 alongside krypton and xenon, this noble gas gets its name from the Greek word for 'new' and glows bright red in electrical discharge — what element is it?
Neon: Chemical element with atomic number 10 (Ne)
This Turkish-born American economist, a Harvard-trained NYU professor, earned lasting fame as one of the few who foresaw the 2008 subprime mortgage crisis. Who is he?
With atomic number 76 and symbol Os, this bluish-white transition metal has the highest density of any stable element and was once prized for fountain-pen nib tips — what is it?
Osmium: Chemical element with atomic number 76 (Os). Osmium (from Ancient Greek ὀσμή (osmḗ) 'smell') is a chemical element; it has symbol Os and atomic number 76.

First described by a 17th-century French mathematician in 1653, this fluid mechanics principle states that a pressure change at any point in a confined, incompressible fluid is felt equally throughout it — what's it called?
Pascal's law: Principle in fluid mechanics. The law was established by French mathematician Blaise Pascal in 1653 and published in 1663.
Named from a Tupi-Guarani word for tobacco filtered through French, this South American flowering plant genus is a garden hybrid favorite — which plant?
Petunia: Genus of flowering plants. The popular flower of the same name derived its epithet from the French, which took the word pétun, 'tobacco', from a Tupi–Guarani language.

Often stereotyped as ferocious predators, these South American freshwater fish actually have varied diets that include plant matter, making them more omnivorous than their reputation suggests. What fish are they?
Piranha: Common name for certain fishes of the family Serrasalmidae.
Chickens, turkeys, ducks, and geese all fall under this term for birds domesticated for meat, eggs, or feathers — what is it called?
Poultry: Domesticated birds kept by humans for their eggs, meat or feathers.
Forming the front-most part of the hip bone in vertebrates, this structure is made up of a superior ramus, an inferior ramus, and a body — which bone?
Pubis: Most forward-facing of the three main regions making up the os coxa.
Roughly 12 centimeters long in adults, this final section of the large intestine temporarily stores waste before it passes into the anal canal — what is it?
Rectum: Final portion of the large intestine. The rectum (pl.: rectums or recta) is the final straight portion of the large intestine in humans and some other mammals, and the gut in others.
Having spent years building theremins, this engineer debuted the first commercial synthesizer in 1964 and later the portable Minimoog — earning a spot in the Inventors Hall of Fame. Who is it?
Robert Moog: American electronic music pioneer (1934–2005)

The largest living reptile, whose males can top 1,000 kg and stretch six metres, ranges from India's coast through Southeast Asia to northern Australia — and earns its 'dangerous to humans' reputation. Which croc is it?
Saltwater crocodile: Species of reptile. It has been listed as Least Concern on the IUCN Red List since 1996.
As chief technology officer of a Turkish defense company, this pilot-engineer designed Turkey's first indigenous unmanned combat aerial vehicle and its first unmanned fighter jet. Who is he?
Selçuk Bayraktar: Turkish engineer and businessman. Selçuk Bayraktar (born 7 October 1979) is a Turkish pilot, engineer and businessman.
Related to polecats but more closely kin to the Old World stink badgers, these black-and-white mammals defend themselves by spraying a foul-smelling liquid from their anal glands — which animal?
Skunk: Common name of mammals in the family Mephitidae.
Acting as a blood filter and red-blood-cell recycling center, which vertebrate organ also stores a reserve of blood for use during hemorrhagic shock?
Spleen: Immune organ that filters blood.
NATO calls it 'Frogfoot' but its Soviet designers named it after the rook; this subsonic twin-engine jet first flew in 1975 to give close air support to ground forces — which aircraft?
Sukhoi Su-25: Soviet attack aircraft introduced 1978.
Once the thylacine went extinct in 1936, this stocky, screeching marsupial — now confined to a single island — became the world's largest carnivorous marsupial; what is it?
Tasmanian devil: Australian carnivorous marsupial. The Tasmanian devil (Sarcophilus harrisii; palawa kani: purinina) is a carnivorous marsupial of the family Dasyuridae.
In tetrapods this body region between the neck and abdomen houses the heart, lungs, and thymus gland, while in insects and crustaceans it forms one of three main body segments — what is it called?
Thorax: Frontal part of an animal's body, between its head and abdomen.
Usually caused by a new genetic mutation rather than inherited, which disorder produces deformities of the ears, eyes, cheekbones, and chin but typically leaves intelligence normal?
Treacher Collins syndrome: Human genetic disorder. The degree to which a person is affected may vary from mild to severe.
Roughly 20 to 30 centimeters long in adults, this smooth-muscle tube carries urine from each kidney down to the bladder — what is it called?
Ureter: Tubes used in the urinary system in most animals.
Known as the 'true foxes,' animals in this genus are smaller and bushier-tailed than any wolf or jackal, with a signature dark triangular mask between the eyes — which genus?
Vulpes: Genus of true foxes. The members of this genus are colloquially referred to as true foxes, meaning they form a proper clade.
Made up of eight carpal bones and home to the carpal tunnel and the anatomical snuff box, this joint connects the hand to the forearm — which body part?
Wrist: Part of the arm between the lower arm and the hand.
The symbol for carbon is C. Carbon is a chemical element; it has symbol C and atomic number 6.
What is the chemical symbol for hafnium?
The symbol for hafnium is Hf. Hafnium is a chemical element; it has symbol Hf and atomic number 72.
